title: Improving the sustainability of water resources and irrigated agriculture in the Ararat Plain (AFD loan for Vedi reservoir) and EU Irrigated Agriculture Development in Ararat and Armavir Marzes (IADAAM)
summary: AFD finances the Vedi reservoir (29 million m3) and modernisation of the irrigation network for about 3,200 ha in the Ararat Plain, while an EU grant (IADAAM) delivered by AFD supports institutional reform, farmer advisory teams and drip/sprinkler irrigation pilots in Ararat and Armavir marzes. The reservoir is reported as built in 2026; IADAAM implementation was extended to December 2027.
activities: Construction of the Vedi reservoir (29 million m3 storage, gravity irrigation, expected 12.2 million kWh/yr energy saving) and nine filtration stations
Rehabilitation, modernisation and extension of the irrigation network over about 3,200 ha
IADAAM: institutional support to Ministry of Economy, three pilot agro-technical advisory teams in the two marzes, farmer training, co-financing grant guidelines, land-consolidation studies
Drip and sprinkler irrigation pilots on up to 2,000 ha in Ararat marz and the Baghramyan and Norakert communities of Armavir marz
results: Reservoir construction reported complete in 2026; first phase stored 1.6 million m3 (press report, not opened); nine filtration stations built, awaiting water testing (Ministry of Economy)

title: World Bank Irrigation Development Project (with Additional Financing)
summary: The project rehabilitated critical irrigation structures, converted three pump-fed irrigation schemes to gravity supply and helped set up Water User Associations and water-supply agencies under participatory irrigation management. The Additional Financing (2008) scaled up WUA support and rehabilitation of additional tertiary systems and extended closing to March 2009.
activities: Rehabilitation of critical irrigation structures: Araks river intake of the Armavir scheme, Hoktemberyan main conveyance canal, Myasnikyan secondary canal, and 69 emergency structures in the Shirak, Armavir, Talin, Arzni-Shamiram, Vayots Dzor and Vorotan irrigation systems
Conversion from pumping to gravity irrigation in the Yeghegnadzor, Aygedzor and Ayrum schemes
Institutional development: establishment of Water User Associations (18 WUAs on 47,355 ha in 2003, 36 more on 86,035 ha in 2004) and consolidation of the Water Supply Agency
Water-management accounting software introduced in 33 WUAs
results: Araks intake capacity raised from 27 to 53 m3/s (completed April 2004)
Actually irrigated area rose from 113,400 ha (2004) to 128,600 ha (2008)
Irrigation fee collection rose by about 1,232 million AMD (55.7 percent) between 2004 and 2008
Electricity use fell from 119.2 to 110.3 million kWh (2004 to 2008)

title: Community-based models for biodiversity protection in ecological corridors, Armenia (WWF Armenia; BMZ/KfW Eco-Corridor Fund)
summary: WWF Armenia sets up community-based conservation models in ecological corridors, financed by BMZ through KfW's Ecoregional Corridor Fund. Communities sign up to ten-year nature-conservation agreements based on jointly developed land-use plans and receive annual compensation and small investments. In Armenia, agreements were signed with communities in Lori, Syunik, Vayots Dzor and Ararat.
activities: Ten-year nature-conservation agreements with community environmental NGOs, backed by land-use plans
Annual compensation payments and small investments (e.g. solar PV on community buildings)
Wildlife monitoring with community guardians (leopard, bezoar goat, mouflon, bear)
results: Four tripartite environmental agreements signed with Sisian, Vayk, Yeghegis and Ararat communities (Ecolur, Nov 2023)
Pambak community, Lori: 7,938 ha community-based environmental zone agreed 17 Jun 2024 (main zone 1,776 ha; sustainable-management zone 6,162 ha)
Across Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia, 20 community organisations had signed conservation agreements by the KfW evaluation

title: KfW Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) Akhuryan River - Kaps reservoir and gravity irrigation (Phases I and II)
summary: KfW finances completion of the Kaps reservoir on the Akhuryan River (first phase 25 million m3, later expandable to 60 million m3) and a gravity irrigation system replacing pumped irrigation in Shirak and Talin, together with river-basin management planning and irrigation-institution support. Works stalled after the contractor's contract was terminated and a new project design and tender are being prepared (press, 2026).
activities: Construction of the Kaps dam/reservoir and auxiliary structures, restoration of the Kumayri irrigation tunnel and gravity irrigation pipe system
Relocation of Jradzor village (partly or fully submerged by the reservoir)

Consulting for accompanying measures: river basin management plan, water-balance computer models, monitoring, WUA and irrigation institutions, agricultural productivity and value chains, support for operation of the Kaps and Arpi dams
ESIA expert services (Phase I grant)

title: FAO assistance for a National Forest Monitoring and Assessment System (NFMAS) in Armenia
summary: FAO has supported Armenia in building a national system to monitor and assess forests since 2022, including nationwide field-data collection and, from 2025-2026, an SDC-funded project to establish a dedicated National Forest Monitoring Unit and run continuous cycles of a national forest inventory. Armenia has not conducted a full national forest inventory since the 1980s.
activities: Nationwide field data collection system for forest monitoring (2023-2025 phase)
Establish a National Forest Monitoring Unit, training and knowledge transfer
Continuous cycles of National Forest Inventory combined with remote sensing and GIS
Monitoring of reforestation, afforestation and agroforestry and their effectiveness
results: NFMA methodology developed and operationalised; Collect Earth survey of Armenia's land categories completed; Year-1 field data 100% collected, Year-2 50% (FAO fact sheet, Oct 2025, under the FAO/GCF project)

title: Community-based conservation and adaptation to climate change in Syunik region (NABU Armenia; IATI: Community based nature conservation and climate adaption as a contribution to poverty reduction in Armenia)
summary: A BMZ-funded NABU Armenia project that supported community-based nature conservation and climate adaptation in rural Syunik. It ran consultations and a small-grant contest on climate adaptation, water, rural tourism, organic agriculture and pasture management, and distributed 15,000 trees to residents of 35 communities.
activities: Consultations and small-grant contest on climate adaptation, sustainable use of natural resources, rural tourism, organic agriculture and pasture management
Distribution of 15,000 trees to residents; community parks created in Uits and at Zorats Karer reserve
results: 35 communities included; 15,000 trees presented to residents; parks created in Uits and on the Zorats Karer reserve territory, parks planned in four more communities (NABU Armenia)

title: Local Empowerment of Actors for Development (LEAD) in Lori and Tavush regions
summary: LEAD applied the EU LEADER approach in Lori and Tavush: five Local Action Groups were set up, prepared local development strategies and funded business and community initiatives, with FAO supporting partnership building, territorial cooperation and local governance. The programme also fed national territorial development planning.
activities: Establish five Local Action Groups (Tashir+, Lorva Dzor, Gandzor, Aghstevi Hovit, Tsili Tsov) and territorial offices
Participatory local development strategies and action plans
Grants to local businesses and community initiatives; post-COVID recovery support
Emergency aid after the June 2024 floods
results: 196 business and 34 community initiatives supported; more than 150 new jobs; more than 3,000 people trained (UNDP/EU closing, Dec 2025)
Five LAG territorial offices established and five LAGs registered as NGOs with Strategic Action Plans

title: Building Armenia's national transparency framework under the Paris Agreement (CBIT) and CBIT 2
summary: Two consecutive GEF-funded, UNDP-implemented projects that build Armenia's institutional and technical capacity to meet the enhanced transparency requirements of the Paris Agreement. CBIT 1 (2020-2025) developed arrangements for measuring, reporting and verifying mitigation policies and greenhouse-gas data; CBIT 2 (approved January 2026) continues this work.
activities: National greenhouse-gas inventory and reporting capacity for Article 13 transparency
MRV arrangements and data-collection methodology for mitigation policies and actions
Inter-agency coordination for climate data and reporting
results: Methodology for mitigation-MRV data requirements and collection developed by Gauss International Consulting (workshop of 30 Sep 2022, attended by over 45 representatives of ministries and agencies)

title: Forest Restoration and Climate Change in Armenia (FORACCA, Swiss SDC)
summary: SDC-funded programme led by the Swiss WSL institute with the Forest Alliance of Armenia (four NGOs) and FAO. At national level it strengthens forest management, forest monitoring and climate-adaptation data; at local level it supports community forestry, afforestation on community lands and agroforestry in selected villages.
activities: Afforestation and maintenance of young forest on community lands (236 ha across four 2025 sites)
Agroforestry systems and windbreaks in four marzes, designed with the Armenian National Agrarian University
National forest monitoring (FAO-led National Forest Monitoring Unit) and climate scenarios / local climate impact profiles
results: 2025: 722,482 trees planted; 142 ha new forest at Lernajur 4 (60 ha SDC-financed); 70 ha maintained at Lernajur 1 and 2 (My Forest Armenia report)

title: Sustainable water management for resilient community development in Armenia (EU4Sevan+; BMZ, GIZ, EU)
summary: Successor to EU4Sevan. It helps selected municipalities in the extended Lake Sevan catchment provide eco-friendly and climate-friendly water and wastewater services, through policy and legal reform, municipal action plans, pilot decentralised and nature-based wastewater treatment, and training of authorities.
activities: Improve policy, legal and financing framework for water and wastewater
Municipal action plans and investment programmes; pilot decentralised and nature-based wastewater solutions
Training of authorities in integrated water-body management and basin planning; civil-society and public-awareness work
results: Field mission (July 2026) evaluated pilot sites in Lechap, Sarukhan and Lusakunk (Gavar and Vardenis municipalities); no system reported built

title: USAID Clean Energy and Water Program (CEWP)
summary: USAID programme (fall 2011 to September 2015) giving technical support for integrated energy and water planning at sub-basin level, advising on hydropower and water regulation and running small community-level pilots. It produced basin management plans for the Vorotan, Voghji and Meghriget rivers (Southern basin).
activities: Technical assistance for integrated energy and water planning; basin management plan for the Southern basin
Biological monitoring in the Vorotan river basin
Community pilots: solar and heating at Darbas polyclinic, LED street lighting in Armavir region, solar energy for an orphanage, a rural water project
results: Basin management plan for the Vorotan, Voghji and Meghriget basins, later adopted by the government (search coverage; ME&A news)

title: Irrigation System Modernization Project (Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development / Eurasian Development Bank) and WB-administered preparation grant
summary: A USD 40 million EFSD (EDB-managed) soft loan financed a five-year project to build or restore eight gravity irrigation systems and improve Water User Association management. The World Bank administered a USD 495,000 grant (2014-2015) that prepared the feasibility study, safeguards framework and WUA capacity studies.
activities: Build or restore eight gravity irrigation systems totalling 70.4 km (8.1 km main canals, 54.1 km inter-farm canals, 277.8 km on-farm canals)
Strengthen WUA responsibility and management
Preparation grant: feasibility study, ESMF, WUA institutional and technical capability studies, additional project documents

title: Land Restoration and Ecosystem Service Improvement through Use of Fruit and Nut Tree Biodiversity in Armenia (UNEP/GEF 11140)
summary: A UNEP-implemented, GEF-8 medium-size project executed by the Forest Committee of the Ministry of Environment. It aims to contribute to landscape restoration by using Armenia's indigenous fruit and nut tree biodiversity to improve ecosystem services, food security and rural livelihoods.
activities: Landscape assessment to identify priority degraded areas and select sites (per WWF/UNEP project descriptions found via search)
Demonstration and pilot restoration sites with indigenous fruit and nut tree species in communal and degraded areas
Biodiversity and climate-adaptation knowledge centre and information system

title: USAID Participatory Utilization and Resource Efficiency of Water (PURE-Water) Activity
summary: A USAID civic-engagement activity to reduce groundwater abstraction in the Ararat Valley and raise water productivity and efficiency through public awareness, citizen participation in oversight of water management, and small-scale infrastructure. A 2018 partnership with Coca-Cola Hellenic Armenia ran outreach for Ararat Valley residents.
activities: Public awareness campaigns and citizen participation in water-resource oversight; policy and regulatory improvements for responsible water use
Design of small-scale infrastructure projects
Survey and stakeholder analysis of water usage in Ararat Valley communities (2017)

title: Regional Rapid Response Teams for a decentralized Rescue System in Armenia (phases I and II)
summary: SDC created, trained and equipped five Regional Rapid Response Teams so that Armenia's rescue system could respond to earthquakes and other disasters outside Yerevan. Between 2013 and 2016 the project trained 235 team members; the Yerevan team passed INSARAG external classification in 2015.
activities: Create, train and equip five regional rapid response (urban search and rescue) teams
Upgrade capacity towards INSARAG 'medium rescue' level
results: 235 team members trained 2013-2016; Yerevan team INSARAG-classified in 2015; all teams passed domestic classification (Regional Post)

title: IFAD Infrastructure and Rural Finance Support Programme (IRFSP)
summary: IRFSP improves rural water supply and small and medium irrigation networks in poor mountain marzes and provides rural finance countrywide, to cut rural poverty especially among women and youth. OPEC Fund reports works on around 3,200 ha in 35 communities and about 78,000 expected beneficiaries.
activities: Develop small and medium-scale irrigation distribution systems (about 3,200 ha in 35 communities)
Rural water supply for consumption and agricultural use, coordinated with water management companies
Rural finance component (countrywide)

title: Strengthening Forest Monitoring (World Bank trust-fund grant P109572 / TF092157)
summary: World Bank trust-fund grant to strengthen Armenia's forest institutions' capacity to combat illegal logging and other forest violations, centred on the State Forest Monitoring Center. It also aimed to create a model of public awareness and participation in monitoring illegal use of forest resources.
activities: Build capacity for forest monitoring in the State Forest Monitoring Center
Develop new systems and procedures for effective forest monitoring
Public awareness and participation in combating illegal forest use

title: IFAD Rural Asset Creation Programme (RACP)
summary: RACP created a vertically integrated fruit and nut sector by establishing Fruit Armenia JSC and planting orchards in the poor border marzes of Tavush, Vayots Dzor and Talin district of Aragatsotn. A second component financed community water supply, gas and access roads in seven mountainous marzes.
activities: Establish Fruit Armenia JSC and orchards (fruits and nuts) with smallholder links
Rural infrastructure: community water supply, gas, drainage structures, access to orchards and markets (OFID financing)

title: R2D Syunik - Recovery, Resilience, Development for Syunik (Team Europe Initiative)
summary: R2D Syunik supports micro, small and medium enterprises and sustainable small-scale green community infrastructure in Syunik marz. Infrastructure choices follow community five-year development plans and EU climate-proofing guidelines.
activities: Component 1: business support, access to finance and markets, human capital (women, youth)
Component 2: small-scale green communal infrastructure under local responsibility (excludes schools and hospitals)

title: EIB Global EUR 50 million loan for development in Syunik province (drinking water, health, education)
summary: EIB Global loan for Syunik province covering reliable drinking water (over 30,000 people), healthcare facilities including polyclinics, and vocational education, with EU and member-state support for preparation. Specific towns and communities are not named in the press release.
activities: Drinking water supply improvements reaching over 30,000 people
Upgrading health facilities and vocational training centres

title: Rural Economic Development - New Economic Opportunities (RED-NEO)
summary: RED-NEO is a USAID cooperative agreement supporting rural entrepreneurship in agriculture and related value chains, with added funding in 2021 for women's economic leadership and mentoring. The implementing partner and community list were not found in sources opened.
activities: Business skills and small grants for rural producers
Mentoring programme for women entrepreneurs (2021 addition)

title: IFAD Farmer Market Access Programme (FMAP)
summary: FMAP provided financial services (loans and venture capital through a dedicated fund) to small and medium rural enterprises and farmers to stimulate commercial activity and diversify rural livelihoods. It operated as a financial-services and enterprise programme rather than a geographically bounded infrastructure project.
activities: Financial services for small and medium-scale rural enterprises and farmers
